
This vignette demonstrates plotting diagnostics for a fitted model.

```{r}
library(PharmaStatsR)
set.seed(123)
example_data <- data.frame(
  SubjectID = rep(1:5, each = 2),
  Time = rep(0:1, times = 5),
  DV = rnorm(10),
  WT = rnorm(10, 70, 5)
)
model <- fit_covariate_model(example_data, "DV", "SubjectID", "Time")
```

## Observed vs Predicted

```{r, fig.alt="Observed responses against fitted values with an identity line."}
plot_obs_vs_pred(model, example_data)
```

## Residuals

```{r, fig.alt="Raw and normalized residuals plotted against observation time."}
plot_residuals(model)
```

## Binned observed and fitted values

`plot_vpc()` plots the observed 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles together with
the median fitted value in each time bin. Its ribbon describes the observed
data, not predictive uncertainty. No new observations are simulated; a formal
simulation-based visual predictive check requires a separate workflow.

```{r, fig.alt="Observed percentile ribbon and fitted medians across time bins."}
plot_vpc(model, example_data, bins = 2)
```

## Export a report

`generate_report()` combines parameter estimates and diagnostic plots into an
HTML or PDF file. Supply the fitted model and its diagnostic data:

```{r eval=FALSE}
report_path <- generate_report(
  model, example_data,
  output_file = "reports/analysis.html"
)
pdf_path <- generate_report(
  model, example_data,
  output_format = "pdf_document",
  output_file = "reports/analysis.pdf"
)
```

Relative paths are resolved from the working directory in which you call the
function. Absolute paths are also accepted, and missing parent directories are
created. If you omit a filename extension, the renderer adds one for the chosen
format. The return value is the absolute path of the file actually produced;
existing files at that destination may be overwritten. A directory alone is
not a valid output filename.

With `output_file = NULL`, the report is saved to a temporary file. Rendering
uses a separate temporary copy of the installed template, so it does not
require write access to the package directory. Intermediate files are cleaned
up after success or failure. HTML includes its plot images; PDF requires a
LaTeX installation in addition to Pandoc. Both formats require `rmarkdown`.
